state.goal: Choose authentication state for a browser-based staff portal
state.question: Which authentication state scheme fits the account revocation policy?
known_constraints: staff must remain signed in across application restarts
evidence: Scenario AUTH baseline: there are no non-browser clients; either design can use secure cookies and survive application restarts.
Scenario AUTH baseline: a durable session store may be added; the pure JWT design validates signature and a 60-minute expiry locally, without introspection, denylist, or per-account state.
Scenario AUTH baseline: the security owner has not specified whether account disablement must revoke existing credentials immediately or may wait until expiry.
JWT expiration claim semantics are defined in RFC 7519 section 4.1.4: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7519.html#section-4.1.4
Scenario AUTH confirmed: account disablement must invalidate the next authenticated request immediately, including credentials issued earlier; waiting for token expiry is forbidden.

Scenario AUTH confirmed: the session design checks the durable session row on every request; disabling an account synchronously deletes all its session rows. The JWT alternative remains strictly stateless.

alternatives.name: Durable server-side sessions
alternatives.description: Secure cookie carries an opaque session identifier; each request looks up a durable server-side row. Account disablement can delete rows.
disadvantages: requires a durable session store and a lookup on each request

alternatives.name: Purely local JWT validation
alternatives.description: Secure cookie carries a signed token valid for 60 minutes; validate signature and expiry only, with no revocation lookup.
disadvantages: previously issued tokens remain accepted until expiry under this design
